chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about touching the Stone from the side of the Door. He said: 'Is it not that you intend to touch the Corner?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'It will suffice for you whatever your hand can reach.'

key_terms.اسْتِلَامُ: Touching/kissing the Stone as a ritual act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on touching the Black Stone if one cannot reach it directly?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of *Istilam* by distinguishing between the physical Black Stone and the Yamani Corner (*Rukn al-Yamani*), noting that the pilgrim's intent is often directed toward the latter. He establishes that the ritual is fulfilled as long as the hand reaches the stone, emphasizing the flexibility (*rukhsa*) in the physical act of touching during the crowded circumambulation (*Tawaf*). This highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the spirit of the act and practical ease for worshippers.
